from src.slugify import slugify

cases = [
    ('  Hello World  ', 'hello-world'),
    ('Hello   World', 'hello-world'),
    ('Hello\tWorld\nAgain', 'hello-world-again'),
    ('   ', ''),
    ('\t\n ', ''),
    ('Hello, World!', 'hello,-world!'),
    ('  A  B  C  ', 'a-b-c'),
    ('Title', 'title'),
]
for inp, expected in cases:
    got = slugify(inp)
    status = 'OK' if got == expected else 'FAIL'
    print(f'{status}: {inp!r} -> {got!r} (expected {expected!r})')
"

steps.description: Fix src/slugify.py so leading and trailing whitespace is ignored, every run of whitespace becomes one hyphen, whitespace-only input returns an empty string, and punctuation is preserved.

changes: Changed src/slugify.py to use value.lower().split() instead of value.strip().lower().split(" "), so str.split() with no separator collapses any run of whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines) into single tokens, ignores leading/trailing whitespace, returns [] for whitespace-only input (joining to an empty string), and leaves punctuation intact.
arguments.rationale: Using split() without an argument is the idiomatic fix: it splits on arbitrary runs of whitespace, trims leading/trailing whitespace implicitly, and yields an empty list for whitespace-only strings, satisfying all four requirements while preserving punctuation.
risks: Behavior now also collapses tabs/newlines (broader than just spaces), which matches the 'every run of whitespace' requirement. Punctuation remains preserved as-is.
arguments.root_cause: The original implementation split on literal single spaces (split(\" \")), which failed to collapse runs of multiple spaces/tabs/newlines into one hyphen and could leave embedded whitespace or produce double hyphens. Additionally, strip() only removed edge whitespace but didn't help interior runs.
